info.name: EventHub-A2 full API
info.description:
IFN636 Assessment 2, EventHub. Every backend endpoint, with the error cases alongside the successes.

The collection covers all four team features, not one of them: bookings and refunds (folder 3, FR-01 to FR-03), event discovery (folder 2, FR-04 to FR-06 and FR-11), reviews and ratings (folder 4, FR-07 and FR-08), and notifications with the audit trail (folders 5 and 6, FR-09, FR-10 and NFR-04). 57 requests, 102 assertions.

HOW TO RUN
1. Seed the fixtures the API will not create for itself: cd backend, then node scripts/seedDemoFixtures.js. It creates the admin, a finished event and a confirmed booking, and prints the ids. See postman/README.md.
2. Set baseUrl, either http://localhost:5001 or the deployed address.
3. Set seedEventId, seedPassword and adminToken from step 1. For adminToken, log in once as admin@eventhub.test and copy the token from the response. The admin login is deliberately not a request here, so no administrator credential sits in a committed file.
4. Run the folders in order. The tests save the tokens and ids each later folder needs, so nothing has to be pasted by hand.

Reruns: folder 4 leaves a review behind and one review per customer per event is enforced by a unique index, so a second full run answers 409 where the first answered 201. Reseed before repeating a full run.

Author: Nikhittha Mukkala

item.name: 4. Reviews (FR-07, FR-08)
item.description:
Reviews on events that have already finished, and the guards around who may leave one.

This folder needs the seeded fixtures: a past event and a confirmed booking for reviewer@eventhub.test. Run backend/scripts/seedDemoFixtures.js once against whichever database you are pointing at, then set seedEventId, reviewerEmail and seedPassword from what it prints. The demo server in member4/demo-server does this for you.

Run the folder against a freshly seeded database. The first request leaves a review, so a second run on the same data finds it already there and the 201 becomes a 409.

item.name: 6. Audit trail (FR-10, NFR-04, US-4.3)
item.description:
My feature. The Singleton AuditLogger's output, read back through the admin only endpoint.

The 200 requests need an admin account. There is no way to register one on purpose, so create it directly in MongoDB and put its token in the adminToken variable. The 401 and 403 requests run without it.
